proved: Inspection derives one SHA-256 repair revision from exact recognized active/archive/quarantine locations, Drive IDs, names, sizes, and raw content hashes but returns only the revision and bounded counts.
Repair accepts only the exact inspection revision and fails before writing if the inventory changed.
The maximal recoverable event graph repeatedly removes missing-parent events and refuses more than 5,000 events or 20 tips rather than inventing or adjudicating history.
A canonical content-addressed recovery snapshot is appended or reused before any active record moves.
The complete pre-existing inventory is re-read after snapshot creation; an unexpected concurrent record or changed/missing record causes zero moves.
Invalid active records move to a recoverable quarantine folder, valid active records return to the recoverable archive, invalid archived records remain untouched, and no path deletes records.
A later inspection includes quarantine: valid parent-complete quarantined records can contribute to a new recovery snapshot while malformed quarantine remains untouched and untrusted.
MCP starts inspection and repair as four-slot background jobs, returns immediately, heartbeats every 30 seconds, and exposes count-only polling without Drive IDs or title/author/body content.
notProved: A real Google Drive repair, interruption at every HTTP boundary, quota/rate-limit behavior, or recovery after GUI/process loss.
Physical two-install observation of repair propagation or a packaged build exposing all 42 tools.
Cancellation of an in-flight title-repair job through MCP; the underlying Tauri invocation has no cancellation channel and is bounded by the native 120-second deadline.
That quarantined records are malicious rather than damaged, or that any recovered title is true or appropriately adjudicated.
Automatic repair, archive deletion/retention policy, more than 20 competing tips, or histories beyond the documented file/event/byte bounds.
A shipped updater artifact containing this checkpoint.
